## Investigation

Can macOS recognize the controller while the host has no network connection and
no ROLI application is running?

::: {.manual-prereq title="Confirm the protected baseline exists"}

Confirm `../evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-baseline.yml` exists and says
that no device configuration has been changed. Close ROLI Dashboard and any
other vendor software before connecting the device. Keep the approved
preservation-investigation specification active; if its scope changes, pause and
revise the specification before proceeding.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Create the offline observation record"}

Disconnect the Mac from Wi-Fi and Ethernet. Record the time and method in a new
file:

```bash
cp evidence/templates/offline-connection.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-offline-connection.yml
```

Then connect the Seaboard Block by USB. In Audio MIDI Setup, inspect the MIDI
Studio view and record the displayed device name, whether it appears, and any
visible ports. Do not alter device configuration.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Preserve a minimal host observation"}

If useful, save a redacted screenshot of the MIDI Studio view beside the
record. Do not include unrelated devices, account information, or serial
numbers. If no device appears, record that absence and the cable/port used;
absence is a result, not a reason to try a firmware update.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Evaluate offline recognition"}

Mark the record `confirmed` only if the controller appeared in macOS while the
network was disconnected and no vendor tool was running. Otherwise mark it
`not-confirmed` and record the exact visible symptom. This stage answers only
operating-system recognition; it does not yet establish MIDI output.

:::
